## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks

1	//! [`BedrockModelBuilder`] — fluent constructor for [`crate::BedrockModel`].
2	//!
3	//! ## Credentials / AWS config laziness
4	//!
5	//! The synchronous [`BedrockModelBuilder::build`] only validates the model-id
6	//! and assembles a Bedrock SDK [`Client`]; it **does not** make any network
7	//! call and **does not** verify your AWS credentials.  Credential/auth
8	//! failures surface later, at invoke time, as a
9	//! [`paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError`].
10	//!
11	//! [`BedrockModel::from_env`] loads the SDK config from the environment (an
12	//! `async` operation because it may fetch IMDS/SSO tokens), but the same
13	//! credential-laziness rule applies: loading the config does not prove the
14	//! credentials will be accepted by Bedrock.
15	
16	use std::sync::Arc;
17	
18	use aws_config::Region;
19	use aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::Client;
20	use paigasus_helikon_core::ModelCapabilities;
21	
22	use crate::capabilities::caps_for;
23	use crate::family::ModelFamily;
24	use crate::policy::{ForcedChoicePolicy, OutputPath};
25	
26	// ── BuildError ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	/// Errors that can occur while building a [`crate::BedrockModel`].
29	///
30	/// Runtime errors (auth failures, throttling, …) are reported through
31	/// [`paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError`] at invoke time, not here.
32	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
33	#[non_exhaustive]
34	pub enum BuildError {
35	    /// No AWS SDK client or `SdkConfig` was supplied and `from_env` was not
36	    /// used.  Call `.client(…)`, `.sdk_config(…)`, or use
37	    /// [`crate::BedrockModel::from_env`].
38	    #[error("no AWS client or SdkConfig provided")]
39	    MissingClient,
40	
41	    /// The model identifier was empty.  Pass a non-empty Bedrock model id such
42	    /// as `"anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0"`.
43	    #[error("model id is empty")]
44	    EmptyModelId,
45	}
46	
47	// ── Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
48	
49	/// Resolved builder configuration held by [`crate::BedrockModel`].
50	///
51	/// Cheaply clonable via `Arc` — the `BedrockModel` holds `Arc<Config>` so
52	/// that clone + move into the `'static` stream is zero-copy.
53	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
54	pub(crate) struct Config {
55	    /// Initialized Bedrock SDK client (region already baked in).
56	    pub(crate) client: Client,
57	    /// Bedrock model identifier (e.g. `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`).
58	    pub(crate) model_id: String,
59	    /// Effective model family: the builder override, else the family detected from the model id.
60	    pub(crate) family: ModelFamily,
61	    /// Resolved capability flags for this model instance.
62	    pub(crate) capabilities: ModelCapabilities,
63	    /// Optional default for `max_tokens` when the caller does not set it.
64	    ///
65	    /// When `None` (the default), `inferenceConfig.maxTokens` is omitted from
66	    /// the Bedrock request so that each model applies its own correct limit.
67	    /// Set via [`BedrockModelBuilder::max_output_tokens_default`].
68	    pub(crate) max_output_default: Option<u32>,
69	}
70	
71	/// Build an offline [`Client`] for unit tests. The client makes no AWS call.
72	///
73	/// This function starts its own Tokio runtime, so do not call it from inside
74	/// a runtime.
75	#[cfg(test)]
76	pub(crate) fn offline_client() -> Client {
77	    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
78	        .enable_all()
79	        .build()
80	        .expect("tokio runtime");
81	    rt.block_on(async {
82	        let sdk_cfg = aws_config::defaults(aws_config::BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17())
83	            .region(Region::new("us-east-1"))
84	            .test_credentials()
85	            .load()
86	            .await;
87	        Client::new(&sdk_cfg)
88	    })
89	}
90	
91	/// The effective family: the override when set, else the family from the model id.
92	pub(crate) fn resolve_family(
93	    detected: ModelFamily,
94	    family_override: Option<ModelFamily>,
95	) -> ModelFamily {
96	    family_override.unwrap_or(detected)
97	}
98	
99	/// Make an offline [`Config`] for unit tests. The client makes no AWS call.
100	///
101	/// This function starts its own Tokio runtime, so do not call it from inside
102	/// a runtime.
103	#[cfg(test)]
104	pub(crate) fn offline_config(model_id: &str) -> Config {
105	    let family = resolve_family(ModelFamily::from_model_id(model_id), None);
106	    let capabilities = caps_for(family);
107	    Config {
108	        client: offline_client(),
109	        model_id: model_id.to_owned(),
110	        family,
111	        capabilities,
112	        max_output_default: None,
113	    }
114	}
115	
116	// ── BedrockModelBuilder ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
117	
118	/// Fluent builder for [`crate::BedrockModel`].
119	///
120	/// Start with [`crate::BedrockModel::converse`].
121	///
122	/// ## Credential laziness
123	///
124	/// `build()` is **synchronous** and **does not** contact any AWS endpoint.
125	/// Credential resolution happens inside the SDK client at the first
126	/// invoke call.
127	pub struct BedrockModelBuilder {
128	    model_id: String,
129	    /// Caller-supplied, fully-initialized client (highest precedence).
130	    client: Option<Client>,
131	    /// Caller-supplied `SdkConfig` (used to construct a client when no direct
132	    /// client is injected).
133	    sdk_config: Option<aws_config::SdkConfig>,
134	    /// Optional region override; ignored if a client was injected directly.
135	    region: Option<Region>,
136	    /// Optional capabilities override (wins over the `caps_for` lookup).
137	    capabilities_override: Option<ModelCapabilities>,
138	    /// Optional `max_output_tokens` override.
139	    max_output_override: Option<u32>,
140	    /// Optional family override (wins over detection from the model id).
141	    family_override: Option<ModelFamily>,
142	}

144	impl BedrockModelBuilder {
145	    pub(crate) fn new(model_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
146	        Self {
147	            model_id: model_id.into(),
148	            client: None,
149	            sdk_config: None,
150	            region: None,
151	            capabilities_override: None,
152	            max_output_override: None,
153	            family_override: None,
154	        }
155	    }
156	
157	    /// Inject a pre-constructed Bedrock SDK client.
158	    ///
159	    /// This takes highest precedence.  When a client is injected any
160	    /// `.region(…)` call is **ignored** (the client already has a region baked
161	    /// in) and `.sdk_config(…)` is not used to construct the client either.
162	    pub fn client(mut self, c: Client) -> Self {
163	        self.client = Some(c);
164	        self
165	    }
166	
167	    /// Build the SDK client from a caller-provided [`aws_config::SdkConfig`].
168	    ///
169	    /// Ignored if a direct client was already injected via `.client(…)`.
170	    pub fn sdk_config(mut self, c: &aws_config::SdkConfig) -> Self {
171	        self.sdk_config = Some(c.clone());
172	        self
173	    }
174	
175	    /// Override the AWS region.
176	    ///
177	    /// **Note:** this setting is **ignored** when a client is injected via
178	    /// `.client(…)` because the client already has its region baked in.  The
179	    /// region is only applied when building a client from `.sdk_config(…)` or
180	    /// when using [`crate::BedrockModel::from_env`].
181	    pub fn region(mut self, r: impl Into<Region>) -> Self {
182	        self.region = Some(r.into());
183	        self
184	    }
185	
186	    /// Override the capability flags for this model instance.
187	    ///
188	    /// Wins over the built-in `caps_for` lookup table.
189	    ///
190	    /// It changes only what `capabilities()` reports. It does not change the
191	    /// request. To turn on the family-gated request behavior for an opaque
192	    /// model ID, use [`BedrockModelBuilder::family`].
193	    pub fn capabilities(mut self, c: ModelCapabilities) -> Self {
194	        self.capabilities_override = Some(c);
195	        self
196	    }
197	
198	    /// Set the model family and turn off detection from the model id.
199	    ///
200	    /// The family controls the request translation, the default capabilities
201	    /// and the forced-choice policy, like a detected family. The
202	    /// [`capabilities`](Self::capabilities) override still wins for the
203	    /// reported flags. A second call replaces the first.
204	    ///
205	    /// Use this for opaque model IDs: application inference profiles,
206	    /// provisioned-throughput ARNs and custom-model ARNs. These IDs do not
207	    /// name the family, so detection gives `ModelFamily::Unknown`.
208	    ///
209	    /// With `Anthropic`, `Mistral` or `AmazonNova`, the provider sends
210	    /// `ToolChoice::Required` and `ToolChoice::Tool` on the forced-tool path.
211	    /// Some requests then fail locally:
212	    ///
213	    /// - `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` or `JsonObject` with `ToolChoice::Tool`.
214	    /// - `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` or `JsonObject` with `ToolChoice::None`.
215	    /// - `ToolChoice::Required` with no tools and no `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema`
216	    ///   or `JsonObject`. Each of these formats adds a synthesized tool.
217	    /// - `ToolChoice::Tool` with a name that no tool defines.
218	    ///
219	    /// On the native path, the provider omits these choices and logs a
220	    /// warning. The native path applies to Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5,
221	    /// and to a handle after one rejection.
222	    ///
223	    /// A profile on Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 costs one rejected request
224	    /// for each handle. Build one handle and clone it.
225	    ///
226	    /// ```ignore
227	    /// use paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::{BedrockModel, ModelFamily};
228	    /// # fn f(arn: &str, cfg: &aws_config::SdkConfig) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
229	    /// let model = BedrockModel::converse(arn)
230	    ///     .sdk_config(cfg)
231	    ///     .family(ModelFamily::Anthropic)
232	    ///     .build()?;
233	    /// # Ok(()) }
234	    /// ```
235	    pub fn family(mut self, f: ModelFamily) -> Self {
236	        self.family_override = Some(f);
237	        self
238	    }
239	
240	    /// Override the default `max_output_tokens` passed to Bedrock when the
241	    /// caller does not set `ModelSettings::max_output_tokens`.
242	    pub fn max_output_tokens_default(mut self, n: u32) -> Self {
243	        self.max_output_override = Some(n);
244	        self
245	    }
246	
247	    /// Resolve all settings and construct the [`crate::BedrockModel`].
248	    ///
249	    /// This is **synchronous** — no network calls are made.
250	    ///
251	    /// # Errors
252	    ///
253	    /// - [`BuildError::EmptyModelId`] — model id is an empty string.
254	    /// - [`BuildError::MissingClient`] — neither `.client(…)` nor
255	    ///   `.sdk_config(…)` was called (use [`crate::BedrockModel::from_env`] for
256	    ///   automatic env-based client construction).
257	    pub fn build(self) -> Result<crate::BedrockModel, BuildError> {
258	        // 1. Validate model id.
259	        if self.model_id.is_empty() {
260	            return Err(BuildError::EmptyModelId);
261	        }
262	
263	        // 2. Resolve client.
264	        let client = if let Some(c) = self.client {
265	            // Injected client wins; region override is ignored.
266	            if self.region.is_some() {
267	                tracing::debug!(
268	                    target: "paigasus::bedrock::builder",
269	                    "region() was set but a Client was injected — region override ignored; \
270	                     the injected client's region takes precedence",
271	                );
272	            }
273	            c
274	        } else if let Some(ref sdk_cfg) = self.sdk_config {
275	            if let Some(region) = self.region {
276	                // Region override: build a per-client config that layers the
277	                // override on top of the caller's SdkConfig, then construct
278	                // the client from that config.
279	                let client_cfg = aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::config::Builder::from(sdk_cfg)
280	                    .region(region)
281	                    .build();
282	                aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::Client::from_conf(client_cfg)
283	            } else {
284	                Client::new(sdk_cfg)
285	            }
286	        } else {
287	            return Err(BuildError::MissingClient);
288	        };
289	
290	        // 3. Detect family and resolve capabilities.
291	        let detected = ModelFamily::from_model_id(&self.model_id);
292	        let family = resolve_family(detected, self.family_override);
293	        match self.family_override {
294	            None if family == ModelFamily::Unknown => {
295	                tracing::debug!(
296	                    target: "paigasus::bedrock::builder",
297	                    model_id = %self.model_id,
298	                    "model family not detected from the model id; structured-output synthesis and forced tool choice are off; set BedrockModelBuilder::family to choose the family",
299	                );
300	            }
301	            Some(f)
302	                if detected != ModelFamily::Unknown
303	                    && f != ModelFamily::Unknown
304	                    && detected != f =>
305	            {
306	                tracing::warn!(
307	                    target: "paigasus::bedrock::builder",
308	                    model_id = %self.model_id,
309	                    detected = ?detected,
310	                    family = ?f,
311	                    "the family override differs from the family that the model id names",
312	                );
313	            }
314	            Some(f) => {
315	                tracing::debug!(
316	                    target: "paigasus::bedrock::builder",
317	                    model_id = %self.model_id,
318	                    family = ?f,
319	                    "the model family comes from BedrockModelBuilder::family",
320	                );
321	            }
322	            None => {}
323	        }
324	        let default_caps = caps_for(family);
325	        let capabilities = self.capabilities_override.unwrap_or(default_caps);
326	        let max_output_default = self.max_output_override;
327	
328	        let policy = ForcedChoicePolicy::new(&self.model_id, family);
329	        if policy.path() == OutputPath::Native {
330	            tracing::debug!(
331	                target: "paigasus::bedrock::builder",
332	                model_id = %self.model_id,
333	                "the static rule selects native structured output for this model",
334	            );
335	        }
336	
337	        Ok(crate::BedrockModel {
338	            config: Arc::new(Config {
339	                client,
340	                model_id: self.model_id,
341	                family,
342	                capabilities,
343	                max_output_default,
344	            }),
345	            policy: Arc::new(policy),
346	        })
347	    }
348	}

351	
352	impl crate::BedrockModel {
353	    /// Start building a Bedrock model for the given model id.
354	    ///
355	    /// ```ignore
356	    /// use paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::BedrockModel;
357	    /// # async fn f() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
358	    /// let model = BedrockModel::converse("anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0")
359	    ///     .sdk_config(&aws_config::defaults(aws_config::BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17())
360	    ///         .load().await)
361	    ///     .build()?;
362	    /// # Ok(()) }
363	    /// ```
364	    pub fn converse(model_id: impl Into<String>) -> BedrockModelBuilder {
365	        BedrockModelBuilder::new(model_id)
366	    }
367	
368	    /// Construct a [`crate::BedrockModel`] by loading AWS configuration from
369	    /// the environment (credential files, environment variables, IMDS, SSO…).
370	    ///
371	    /// ## Credential laziness
372	    ///
373	    /// The AWS credential chain is **lazy** — loading the config does not prove
374	    /// that your credentials will be accepted by Bedrock.  Auth/permission
375	    /// failures surface at invoke time as a
376	    /// [`paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError`].
377	    ///
378	    /// ## BehaviorVersion
379	    ///
380	    /// Uses the pinned `BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17()` so that a Dependabot
381	    /// `aws-config` bump cannot silently shift SDK behavior. This version
382	    /// applies the AWS SDK retry behavior from the Retry Behavior 2.1 spec.
383	    /// It also applies a default read timeout to AWS SDK clients.
384	    ///
385	    /// ## Region
386	    ///
387	    /// Pass `None` to use the region from the environment
388	    /// (`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, `~/.aws/config`, …).  Pass `Some(region)` to
389	    /// override it.
390	    pub async fn from_env(model_id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, BuildError> {
391	        Self::from_env_with_region(model_id, None::<Region>).await
392	    }
393	
394	    /// Like [`from_env`][Self::from_env] but with an explicit region override.
395	    pub async fn from_env_with_region(
396	        model_id: impl Into<String>,
397	        region: Option<impl Into<Region>>,
398	    ) -> Result<Self, BuildError> {
399	        let mut loader = aws_config::defaults(aws_config::BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17());
400	        if let Some(r) = region {
401	            loader = loader.region(r.into());
402	        }
403	        let sdk_cfg = loader.load().await;
404	        BedrockModelBuilder::new(model_id)
405	            .sdk_config(&sdk_cfg)
406	            .build()
407	    }
408	}

3	/// Identifies the model family of a Bedrock Converse model ID.
4	///
5	/// The model family selects the capability flags, the schema rewriter rulesets
6	/// and the tool-choice support. The builder detects the family from the model
7	/// ID, or takes it from [`crate::BedrockModelBuilder::family`]. The
8	/// `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute allows future additions without a breaking
9	/// change.
10	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11	#[non_exhaustive]
12	pub enum ModelFamily {
13	    /// Anthropic Claude model family (e.g. `anthropic.claude-*`).
14	    Anthropic,
15	    /// Amazon Nova model family (e.g. `amazon.nova-*`).
16	    AmazonNova,
17	    /// Amazon Titan model family (e.g. `amazon.titan-*`).
18	    AmazonTitan,
19	    /// Meta Llama model family (e.g. `meta.llama*`).
20	    Llama,
21	    /// Mistral model family (e.g. `mistral.mistral-*`).
22	    Mistral,
23	    /// Cohere Command model family (e.g. `cohere.command-*`).
24	    Cohere,
25	    /// Unknown or unrecognized model family.
26	    Unknown,
27	}
28	
29	/// How a model family receives a `ToolChoice::None` request when the
30	/// conversation already holds tool use or tool result blocks.
31	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
32	pub(crate) enum ToolChoiceNoneStrategy {
33	    /// Send the Anthropic `tool_choice: {"type": "none"}` request field.
34	    AnthropicNoneField,
35	    /// Replay the tool history as plain text. Nova rejects the field (P4).
36	    /// The other families are not known to accept it, so they get the text
37	    /// history as a conservative default.
38	    TextHistory,
39	}
40	
41	impl ModelFamily {
42	    /// Detect the model family from a Bedrock model ID.
43	    ///
44	    /// When the first segment is not a known provider name, detection reads
45	    /// the second segment. So a geographic prefix such as `us.`, `eu.`,
46	    /// `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`, `ca.`, `in.` or `global.` is skipped, and a
47	    /// future prefix is skipped too. An ARN is classified by its resource ID
48	    /// (the text after the last `/`). Opaque IDs, such as application
49	    /// inference profile ARNs, give [`ModelFamily::Unknown`]. To set the family for
50	    /// such an ID, use [`crate::BedrockModelBuilder::family`].
51	    ///
52	    /// # Examples
53	    ///
54	    /// ```
55	    /// use paigasus_helikon_providers_bedrock::ModelFamily;
56	    /// assert_eq!(
57	    ///     ModelFamily::from_model_id("anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0"),
58	    ///     ModelFamily::Anthropic,
59	    /// );
60	    /// assert_eq!(
61	    ///     ModelFamily::from_model_id("global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5"),
62	    ///     ModelFamily::Anthropic,
63	    /// );
64	    /// ```
65	    pub fn from_model_id(model_id: &str) -> Self {
66	        let lowered = model_id.to_ascii_lowercase();
67	        let Some(id) = resource_id(&lowered) else {
68	            return Self::Unknown;
69	        };
70	
71	        let (first, rest1) = id.split_once('.').unwrap_or((id, ""));
72	        let (second, rest2) = rest1.split_once('.').unwrap_or((rest1, ""));
73	
74	        Self::classify(first, rest1)
75	            .or_else(|| Self::classify(second, rest2))
76	            .unwrap_or(if first.contains("llama") || second.contains("llama") {
77	                Self::Llama
78	            } else {
79	                Self::Unknown
80	            })
81	    }
82	
83	    /// Map a provider segment (and the text after it) to a family, or `None`
84	    /// when the segment is not a known provider name.
85	    fn classify(provider: &str, rest: &str) -> Option<Self> {
86	        match provider {
87	            "anthropic" => Some(Self::Anthropic),
88	            "amazon" => Some(if rest.starts_with("nova") {
89	                Self::AmazonNova
90	            } else if rest.starts_with("titan") {
91	                Self::AmazonTitan
92	            } else {
93	                Self::Unknown
94	            }),
95	            "meta" => Some(Self::Llama),
96	            "mistral" => Some(Self::Mistral),
97	            "cohere" => Some(Self::Cohere),
98	            _ => None,
99	        }
100	    }
101	
102	    /// Returns `true` when the family supports Bedrock's forced-tool-choice
103	    /// (`toolChoice: { tool: { name } }`) request field.
104	    ///
105	    /// Families that do not support it will have the `tool_choice` field
106	    /// omitted and a `debug!` log emitted instead.
107	    ///
108	    /// Some Anthropic models reject it. See [`rejects_forced_tool_choice`].
109	    pub(crate) fn supports_forced_tool_choice(self) -> bool {
110	        matches!(self, Self::Anthropic | Self::Mistral | Self::AmazonNova)
111	    }
112	
113	    /// Returns the strategy for a `ToolChoice::None` request that carries a
114	    /// tool history.
115	    ///
116	    /// Only Anthropic models accept the `tool_choice: {"type": "none"}` field.
117	    /// Other families get the history as text (probes P4 and P9, spec section 3).
118	    pub(crate) fn tool_choice_none_strategy(self) -> ToolChoiceNoneStrategy {
119	        match self {
120	            Self::Anthropic => ToolChoiceNoneStrategy::AnthropicNoneField,
121	            Self::AmazonNova
122	            | Self::AmazonTitan
123	            | Self::Llama
124	            | Self::Mistral
125	            | Self::Cohere
126	            | Self::Unknown => ToolChoiceNoneStrategy::TextHistory,
127	        }
128	    }
129	}
130	
131	/// Returns the resource ID of a lowercased model ID.
132	///
133	/// For an ARN, this is the text after the last `/`, or `None` when the ARN has
134	/// no `/`. Any other ID is returned unchanged.
135	fn resource_id(lowered: &str) -> Option<&str> {
136	    if lowered.starts_with("arn:") {
137	        lowered.rsplit_once('/').map(|(_, resource)| resource)
138	    } else {
139	        Some(lowered)
140	    }

## Provider tool types

Some providers define their own tool types. The Anthropic memory tool is one example. The provider expects a typed entry that has a type and a name. The entry has no description and no schema. A tool declares such a type with `Tool::provider_types`.

```rust,ignore
use paigasus_helikon::core::ProviderToolType;
use paigasus_helikon::anthropic::PROVIDER_ID;

fn provider_types(&self) -> &[ProviderToolType] {
    &self.types // for example one entry: ProviderToolType::new(PROVIDER_ID, "memory_20250818")
}
```

`ProviderToolType::new(provider, type_name)` names the provider and the type. Call `with_params` to add extra fields for the typed entry.

A tool can declare at most one entry for each provider. The default is an empty slice, so an existing tool does not change.

A tool wrapper must forward `provider_types` from the tool that it wraps. If the wrapper does not forward it, the typed entry is lost and the provider gets the generic schema.

Anthropic is the only provider that uses this declaration now. It sends `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}` for the memory tool. OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock and LiteLLM send the generic schema. See [Model Providers](./model-providers.md).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The approach is sound, and the probes support most rules. One rule makes a valid memory call fail on the native structured-output path. Two `ToolChoice::None` branches are not specified, and the native checks may not count typed tools. Several request shapes that the design depends on have no probe. Fix the BLOCKER and run the missing probes before implementation starts. The fixes are local and do not change approach 1.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **The native anchor makes a valid memory call fail in the stream** - In `build_native` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-844/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/native.rs, lines 105-112), the code adds the synthesized anchor when `structured && all_tools.is_empty() && has_tool_round`. It then sets `synthesizing = true`. If the request has only typed tools, the generic list is empty, so this branch runs. Section 5.7 keeps this behaviour ("When ... the synthesized structured-output tool is in the toolConfig, no placeholder is added"). The model can still call the typed `memory` tool, because the native path never forces a choice. In `finish_events` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-844/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs, lines 325-339), `synthesizing && real_tool_fired` gives `Err("... fired both a real tool and the synthesized output tool ...")`. This also happens when only `memory` fired. The agent gets the `ToolCallDelta`s, then the error, and no `Finish`. | Why it matters: This is the normal memory flow, for example turn 2 after `view` with `JsonSchema` or `JsonObject`. It occurs on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, and on every handle after an SMA-839 fallback. Today a generic `memory` tool makes `all_tools` non-empty, so no anchor is added and the call works. So this is a regression against the generic baseline. It also breaks the goal "structured output on both output paths". | Suggested fix: In `build_native`, count typed tools in the anchor condition (`all_tools.is_empty() && typed.is_empty()`). When typed tools exist, use the 5.7 placeholder with `synthesizing = false`. Add a snapshot: Sonnet 5.5 id, a memory tool round, only the typed tool, `JsonSchema`. Add a stream test: a `memory` call gives `ToolCallDelta` and then `Finish(ToolCalls)`.

### MAJOR
- **`ToolChoice::None` with only typed tools: an early return drops the none field** - `apply_tool_choice_none` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-844/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/tool_choice_none.rs, lines 93-95) returns `unchanged(messages)` with `tool_choice_none: false` when the spec list is empty. Section 5.8 puts the typed names in `seen`. So a history that holds only `memory` calls gives an empty list. A build that follows section 5.8 exactly then sends one of two requests. The first has no `toolConfig`, which gives a 400 error (p5). The second has the anchor but no `tool_choice: none`, so the model can call `memory`. The stream then returns "the model called a tool, but tool_choice is None". Today a generic `memory` tool fills the list and sets the flag. | Why it matters: This is a regression on the exact SMA-833 case that the spec says must keep working. | Suggested fix: State that, with typed tools, the `AnthropicNoneField` outcome always sets the none choice and adds the anchor itself. Use one anchor helper for all three call sites. Add a unit test in tool_choice_none.rs: only a typed `memory` tool and a memory-only history give tools = [placeholder] and none = true. Add a typed variant of `none_shape_is_the_same_on_both_paths`.
- **Native path, `ToolChoice::None` with a structured format: the spec does not cover it** - In `build_native` (native.rs lines 78-80), `None` with a structured format sends no user tools. After a tool round, the synthesized anchor follows, and the request has no none field. The spec does not say if typed tools go out in this branch. If they go out, the model can call `memory`, and `forbid_tool_calls` turns that call into an error. | Why it matters: Two engineers will build different requests, and one of the two requests fails at run time. | Suggested fix: State that this branch sends no typed tools, the same as for user tools. Add a snapshot next to `snap_native_tool_choice_none_json_schema_finalizing_anchor`.
- **The spec does not say that the native-path checks count typed tools** - Section 5.6 puts "The checks also count typed tools" under the forced-tool path only. `build_native` has its own checks: `check_tool_name(&all_tools, name)` (native.rs line 102), and the `Required` error when `all_tools.is_empty() && !structured` (line 119). If these checks keep the generic list only, `Tool { name: "memory" }` fails with "not defined in the tool list". `Required` with only typed tools fails with "requires at least one tool". | Why it matters: Today a generic `memory` tool gives the `ToolOmitted` or `RequiredOmitted` notice instead, so this is a regression. The native test in section 7 does not say "only typed tools", so the test can pass with this bug. | Suggested fix: State that both native checks count typed tools. Add native tests that have only a typed tool, for `Required` and for `Tool { name: "memory" }`.
- **The design relies on request shapes that no probe sent** - (a) An additional `tool_choice: {type: tool, name: X}` where X is in `toolConfig`, for example the synthesized tool or a generic tool. p13 forced only a typed name. Forced structured output with a typed tool depends on this shape on every forced-path Claude model. (b) An additional `{type: any}` when a `toolConfig` is present. p15 had no `toolConfig`, and p8 used `toolConfig.toolChoice`. (c) `outputConfig.textFormat` together with additional `tools`. No probe sent `outputConfig`. This is the only structured-output path on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, and after a fallback. (d) The placeholder together with `tool_choice: none`, `any` or `tool`. p10 sent no choice, and p12 used `weather`, not the placeholder. (e) The placeholder schema. p10 sent `{"type":"object","properties":{}}`, but the spec says `{"type":"object"}`. The risk is low, because the SMA-833 derived spec already uses `{"type":"object"}`. | Why it matters: If (a) or (c) fails, structured output with the memory tool becomes a 400 error, which is an anti-goal. | Suggested fix: Run (a) to (d) with `converse` before implementation, and add the results to section 3. There is also a narrower rule to consider. p11 is a Bedrock-layer check of `toolConfig.toolChoice` against `toolConfig.tools`, and p8 shows that `toolConfig.toolChoice` works when typed tools are present. The narrower rule keeps `toolConfig.toolChoice` for names in `toolConfig`, and for `any` when a `toolConfig` exists. It uses the additional field only for a typed name, for `any` with no `toolConfig` (p15), and for `none` (p12). It keeps the structured-output wire shape of today. It also has one shape with no probe: `toolConfig.toolChoice.tool` when typed tools are present. Probe both rules, then choose one.
- **The live test does not cover the high-risk paths** - Section 7 has one live case: an `Auto` turn 1 and a text turn 2. It does not cover forced structured output with a typed tool.
